title: Testing the security of a device?
description: A user on Reddit's r/cybersecurity subreddit describes a custom hardware device built with a Raspberry Pi Pico and fingerprint sensor that outputs passwords as an HID device. The device employs encrypted password storage, signed firmware with secure boot, and fused read-only keys and debug ports to enhance security. The user seeks external analysis of the firmware repository for potential vulnerabilities, mentioning that the firmware was developed with assistance from an AI tool (claude.ai). No specific vulnerabilities or exploits are reported.

aiSummary: The post details a custom-built hardware password entry device using a Raspberry Pi Pico with a fingerprint sensor. Security features include encrypted password storage, signed firmware with secure boot enforced by a locked key in OTP storage, and a fused debug port to prevent unauthorized access. The firmware source code is publicly available on GitHub, and the user requests a service to analyze the repository for vulnerabilities. No technical details or known vulnerabilities are provided, and no active exploits are reported.
